newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Treasurer disappointed by bankruptcy veto.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Treasurer disappointed by bankruptcy veto.

text.p: California state Treasurer Matt Fong was disappointed by Gov. Pete Wilson's veto of legislation that would have increased state oversight over local governments seeking bankruptcy protection, a spokesman for Fong said on Tuesday.

"Obviously we're disappointed with the governor's veto of the bankruptcy legislation," said Assistant Treasurer Stan Devereux. "We felt that this legislation was necessary to prevent a municipality from making a decision that would certainly impact other parts of the state."
Devereux said he "would not rule out reintroduction of the measure in some form" in the state Legislature next year.

Late on Monday, Wilson vetoed Senate Bill 349, which would have established the Local Agency Bankruptcy Committee. Under the measure, local agencies in the state that intended to file for bankruptcy would have had to seek the committee's approval before petitioning the courts.
Fong had strongly urged Wilson to sign the legislation. Fong argued that the measure could help to lower issuance costs in the state.
The measure was introduced in the wake of Orange County, Calif.,'s unprecedented bankruptcy filing.

Orange County filed for protection under Chapter 9 of the federal Bankruptcy Code on Dec. 6, 1994, after sustaining investment losses of more than $1.6 billion. The county emerged from bankruptcy in June of this year.
The state's Department of Finance was opposed to the legislation.
